learningObjective: Explain prefix caching, its correctness conditions, and its effect on TTFT.

canonicalClaims.claim: Prefix caching stores per-position KV blocks keyed by prompt token ids and reuses them for new requests with matching prefixes; reuse is exact and cuts prefill (and thus TTFT) for the matched prefix length.
conditions: System supports KV block reuse (typically via paged KV).
nonImplications: Does not help without shared prefixes.

misconceptions.claim: Prefix caching stores model output strings.
misconceptions.whyWrong: It stores KV cache blocks, not decoded strings.
Prefix cache is about the prefill; sampling still operates normally on top.

misconceptions.claim: Prefix caching approximates KV via cosine similarity.
misconceptions.whyWrong: It is an exact reuse keyed on token ids; no approximation.

implementationFacts: SGLang uses a radix tree keyed by token ids for O(prefix-len) matching.
vLLM offers 'automatic prefix caching' as an opt-in feature.
performanceScenarios: Long system prompts (few-shot templates, tool-use scaffolds) benefit most.
Per-request unique prompts see no benefit.
